entities.name: Satellite (NASA imagery)
entities.rationale: Hand-drawn satellite icon at top-left; external source of imagery tiles (NASA satellites) feeding the EC2 Spot processing cluster. Not inside any container.

entities.name: EC2 Spot
entities.rationale: Orange icon labeled 'EC2 SPOT' on the left; cluster of spot instances that post-processes incoming satellite tiles and writes outputs to S3 and RDS. Standalone, no container box.

entities.name: S3
entities.rationale: Green bucket icon labeled 'S3' with annotations '10yr, ~5 PB, 100GB/day' above it; stores bulk imagery data, read via HTTP range requests by Fargate and Lambda. Standalone.

entities.name: RDS
entities.rationale: Blue icon labeled 'RDS' below S3; stores metadata mapping tiles to source imagery, queried by Fargate and Lambda. Standalone.

entities.name: ElastiCache (Redis)
entities.rationale: Blue icon labeled 'ELASTICACHE' at top-right; Redis central cache for already-generated tiles, read/written by Fargate. Standalone.

entities.name: AWS Fargate
entities.rationale: Orange icon labeled 'AWS FARGATE' in the center-right; cluster serving web map tiles to users, looks up RDS, reads S3, caches in ElastiCache. Standalone.

entities.name: Lambda
entities.rationale: Orange icon labeled 'LAMBDA' at bottom-right; series of Lambda functions computing time series over a farmer's field area of interest, looking up RDS and reading S3. Standalone.

entities.name: Users (Farmers)
entities.rationale: White users icon to the right of Fargate; farmers/app users who load map tiles from Fargate. The hand-drawn field grid and time-series curve below it represent the farmer-supplied area of interest passed to Lambda. Standalone.

visual_connections.description: Pink curved arrow from the satellite down to EC2 Spot: imagery tiles arrive daily for post-processing.
Pink arrow from EC2 Spot up to S3: processed bulk imagery data is stored in S3.
Pink arrow from EC2 Spot down to RDS: imagery metadata is stored in RDS.
Pink double-headed arrow between S3 and Fargate: Fargate pulls partial objects from S3 using HTTP range requests.
Pink double-headed arrow between RDS and Fargate: Fargate looks up which source imagery corresponds to a tile.
Pink curved double-headed arrow between Fargate and ElastiCache: generated tiles are read from and written to the Redis cache.
Pink double-headed arrow between Fargate and the users icon: users request map tiles and Fargate serves them back.
Thin curved line from S3 down to Lambda: Lambda functions read imagery from S3.
Pink double-headed arrow between RDS and Lambda: Lambda looks up imagery metadata in RDS.
Pink arrow from the hand-drawn field grid / area-of-interest sketch (farmer-supplied) to Lambda: the field boundary is passed to the Lambda functions to compute the time series.
